transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name], nice to meet you. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, so the main reason I’m here is that at work—I'm a registered nurse—on the floor I just lose my train of thought constantly. Like, an IV pump beeps, or someone asks another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I’ve completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on. 

Actually, speaking of the IV pumps, our hospital just switched to this new brand last month and the alarm tone is so high-pitched, it literally pierces through everything. My coworker Jen was just saying how it gives her a headache. She actually transferred from the ICU because she wanted a slower pace, but honestly, our med-surg floor is just as crazy sometimes. We had this one guy last week who kept trying to pull his Foley catheter out, which was a whole ordeal because his daughter was there and she was already so stressed about his diet restrictions... 

But anyway, yeah, it's just... I really struggle to stay on track when there's noise or people talking. I'm sorry, I completely lost where I was going with that. Did that answer your question?
Thinking back, did you have similar problems with distractibility and losing your train of thought when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that's mainly started more recently?

Oh, no, it's definitely not a new thing. It's been like this forever. Even back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing notes on my report cards saying that I was bright but just really careless. I was constantly losing my worksheets, or I'd actually do my homework and then just completely forget to turn it in. My mom had to sit with me every single night just to keep me on track. 

We'd sit at this big oak table in our kitchen... my grandpa actually built that table. He was a carpenter and made almost all the furniture in our house, which is just crazy to think about now because who has the time to build a whole dining set? He made this gorgeous rocking chair too, which I actually still have in my living room. I was just trying to find a new cushion for it at Target the other day, but their home section was completely picked over. I think it's because all the college kids are moving back into the dorms this week. The traffic around the university has been an absolute nightmare because of it, I got stuck behind a U-Haul for like twenty minutes yesterday... 

Wait, I'm sorry. I'm doing it again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, when I was younger. But yeah, I've always been like this, my mom had to watch me do my homework every night.
Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting or speaking impulsively without thinking it through?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm hyper or anything. I can sit still just fine. Actually, I have to sit still for charting all the time, which takes forever. We use Epic at our hospital, and they just pushed this huge update over the weekend that moved all the flowsheets around. It's so frustrating because you finally get used to where everything is, and then they change it. My friend Sarah works at a clinic that still uses paper charts, which sounds like a nightmare, but at least it doesn't crash on you. She was telling me they had a water leak last month and almost lost a bunch of records... 

But anyway, no, I don't feel restless. And I don't really blurt things out or act without thinking. I'm actually pretty quiet, especially in meetings. I just kind of sit there and zone out.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports chronic, pervasive difficulties with attention and distractibility—losing her train of thought with minimal stimuli, forgetting tasks, disorganization—that began in childhood (documented by school reports of carelessness, lost worksheets, forgotten homework) and have persisted into adulthood, causing occupational impairment as a nurse. She explicitly denies hyperactivity, restlessness, or impulsivity, and denies fidgeting or acting without thinking.
